chunks: Ali ibn Hassan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Mihzam entered upon him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Call the maid for us to bring us oil and kohl.' So I called her, and she came with a flask of violet (oil). It was a day of intense cold. So Mihzam poured some of it into his palm, then said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is violet (oil), and this is the intense cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the matter with it, O Mihzam?' He said: 'Our physicians in Kufa claim that the violet (oil) is cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is cold in the summer, soft and hot in the winter.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the temperature of violet oil?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia scholarly appreciation for empirical observation over rigid theoretical classification, as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the Kufan physicians' static humoral diagnosis of violet oil. By noting that the oil feels 'cold' in summer but 'hot' and softening in winter, the Imam demonstrates the relativity of physical properties to environmental context, a nuance often overlooked in contemporary medical theory. This reflects the broader Imami tradition of valuing practical wisdom (*hikmah*) alongside textual and theoretical knowledge.
